page: Microsoft Azure D4pds_v5 is a general-purpose virtual machine based on the 64-bit ARM architecture. Powered by an Ampere ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 processor operating at 3.0 GHz, it supplies 4 dedicated physical cores with a 1:1 thread-to-core mapping, eliminating resource competition inherent in simultaneous multithreading. Memory allocation is configured at 16.0 GB, establishing a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 4.0 GB per core. The instance incorporates 161 GB of local SSD storage, an L3 cache of 32 MB, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and hardware AES cryptographic acceleration.

Benchmark results highlight balanced output in integer compute and memory bandwidth, alongside clear constraints in floating-point and vector processing. The server registers average marks in stress-ng multi-core testing (7,252.87) and single-threaded gzip compression (24.2 GB/sec), with uncached large-block memory read bandwidth achieving 51.33 GB/sec. Conversely, the instance places in lower percentile tiers for single-core execution, yielding a Geekbench single-core score of 1,091 and multi-core score of 3,710. Cryptographic and physics tests reflect the absence of AVX and specialized vector instruction sets on the Neoverse-N1 architecture.

From an infrastructure efficiency perspective, the dedicated physical core architecture provides predictable execution times and lower power overhead characteristic of ARM deployments. Bundled local solid-state storage reduces reliance on external block devices for temporary data caching. The D4pds_v5 is well matched for horizontally scaled web applications, containerized microservices, CI/CD artifact building, and lightweight database management systems recompiled for arm64 environments.
description: Microsoft Azure D4pds_v5 is an arm64 general-purpose instance featuring 4 dedicated physical cores on an Ampere ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 processor running at 3.0 GHz without hyperthreading. It is equipped with 16.0 GB of memory (4.0 GB per core) and includes 161 GB of bundled local SSD storage. Benchmark results show average multi-core throughput in stress-ng and standard gzip compression tasks, but lower relative output in Geekbench single-core and floating-point operations. Large-block memory bandwidth reaches 51.33 GB/sec read and 30.11 GB/sec write speeds. The lack of hardware simultaneous multithreading provides consistent execution times across cores, making it operationally efficient for predictable workloads. With its balanced 1:4 memory allocation and local high-speed disk, the D4pds_v5 serves general-purpose web backends, caching services, software builds, and lightweight relational or document database systems adapted for ARM environments.
